suggestions: Replace the single 40-day price–volume correlation with a dual-horizon blend, e.g., (Corr(Pct(close,10), Pct(volume,10), 20) + Corr(Pct(close,10), Pct(volume,10), 60)) / 2, or Ma(Corr(..., 40), 10). Investment rationale: one rolling correlation window is highly regime-sensitive and can flip sign around volatility breaks, causing the multiplier to invert on unrelated days and eroding year-to-year RankIR (year_pos_frac=0.8); institutional participation persists across weeks and quarters, so averaging short- and long-horizon alignment estimates yields a smoother participation filter and more consistent cross-sectional rankings.

Swap the 10-day spread change for a level-based overextension signal: use Neg(Zscore(Ma((close-vwap)/vwap, 10), 40)) instead of Neg(Diff(Zscore(Ma((close-vwap)/vwap, 10), 40), 10)), still conditioned on price–volume correlation. Investment rationale: Diff on a z-scored spread tracks short-lived acceleration and microstructure noise, which drives high turnover (0.72) and unstable day-to-day IC; mean reversion is better anchored to how far price has sustainably drifted from VWAP rather than how fast that drift is changing, producing a slower-moving state variable that should improve temporal consistency of RankIC.

Stabilize the composite with rank normalization and a participation gate before multiplication, e.g., Rank(Neg(Zscore(Ma((close-vwap)/vwap, 10), 40))) * Max(Rank(Corr(Pct(close,10), Pct(volume,10), 40)), 0), optionally followed by Ma(..., 10). Investment rationale: raw z-score × correlation products amplify outliers when correlation spikes toward ±1 and can flip the signal on negative co-movement days that do not support the VWAP-reversion thesis; cross-sectional ranks and a non-negative correlation floor cap tail sensitivity, while light output smoothing aligns rebalance frequency with the multi-week flow hypothesis and should lift RankIR without reintroducing the short-horizon diff noise already addressed in prior refinements.
